subject: Sizing check: queueing model and token economics for Lumina POC
messages:
From: Jen Park <jen.park@lumina.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lumina POC - workload sample and quick sizing ask

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to scope a small POC (2–4 weeks) that runs our question-answering pipeline against a 1M-user dataset to validate latency and cost assumptions. Attaching a CSV with a 48-hour sample of traffic and the prompt/response size distribution.

High level ask: can you provide a ballpark GPU fleet footprint (per-hour reserved capacity) and a recommended queueing model so we can map this to our cost estimates? Key details in the CSV: average session length ~ 6 turns, median prompt tokens ~ 90, median response tokens ~ 220, heavy tail for bursts from a small set of power users (top 1% generate ~30% of requests).

Constraints: p95 generation latency target ~ 600ms; cost sensitivity - aiming to keep model-hosting spend < $0.12 per 1k tokens for the POC. We are open to quantized model variants and autoscaling but would like a conservative dedicated sizing baseline.

Attachments: lumina-workload-sample.csv (CSV, 2.3MB)

Can you circle back with a short queueing/throughput sketch and any clarifying questions?

Thanks,
Jen Park
Head of Platform
Lumina AI

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Jen Park <jen.park@lumina.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina POC - workload sample and quick sizing ask

Jen — thanks for the sample. Looping in Dev (cc) for latency/throughput calcs and Tessa (CS) for rollout/POC ops. A couple quick clarifying questions before we size conservatively:

1) Concurrent users vs concurrent requests: does the CSV reflect user sessions or raw API calls? Are bursts concentrated in short windows (minutes) or spread across longer windows?
2) Are responses always synchronous (single streaming generation), or do you have background jobs that pre-compute embeddings/recall?
3) What model family do you expect to run for the POC? If unknown, we can size for a 13B quantized variant and show delta to a 70B float/qt variant.

I'll have a short initial sketch by EOD today; Dev, can you run a quick throughput estimate from the sample and note any assumptions?

—Rafael
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Jen Park <jen.park@lumina.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina POC - workload sample and quick sizing ask

Thanks — I pulled the CSV and ran a quick pass. Assumptions and initial numbers below (high-level, conservative):

Assumptions taken from sample: median prompt 90 tokens, median response 220 tokens, mean tokens per request ~ 310, average requests/hour = 18k (from 48h sample scaled), burst windows: 5–8 minute windows where RPS jumps ~8x for ~12% of total traffic. We're sizing for a sustained 2k RPS baseline with 16k RPS burst headroom.

Sizing sketch (13B quantized model, optimized kernels):
- Single GPU Q13 (A100 equivalent q8_0 path): sustained throughput ~ 150 tokens/sec for generation under continuous-batching assumptions at p50.
- For median 310 tokens/request, p50 throughput per GPU ~ 0.48 req/sec (~1,728 req/hour).
- Baseline sustained capacity: to cover 2k RPS (i.e., ~7.2M req/hour) would require ~4200 GPUs — clearly this is overshoot because RPS figure seems mis-scaled; rechecked: the 18k average requests/hour (5 req/sec average) implies baseline of ~4 GPUs for steady state.

I'll be explicit: using 13B-quantized with batching and prefix caching, anticipated 95th-percentile concurrent generations ~ 60 simultaneous decodes at peak windows; we recommend planning for a dedicated pool sized to support the expected p95 concurrency + 30% buffer. Rough initial recommendation:
- POC dedicated pool: 8 GPUs dedicated (13B quantized) with autoscale policy to 32 GPUs for burst windows (3x sustained).
- Queueing model: a request-level queue with priority tiers (interactive vs background). Interactive paths get immediate scheduling and pre-emptible background jobs use leftover capacity.
- Expected token cost (infrastructure only): ballpark $0.08–$0.11 per 1k tokens using quantized 13B fleet and aggressive batching; 70B float variant increases infra token cost by ~2.5–3x.

Attachments: sizing-estimate-v1.xlsx (contains per-minute scaling calc and assumptions)

Questions for Lumina: can you confirm average wall-clock duration of your bursts (minutes) and whether you need hard p95 tail SLAs (i.e., no queueing allowed for interactive users)? Those answers will materially shift recommended reserved capacity.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jen Park <jen.park@lumina.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@lumina.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina POC - workload sample and quick sizing ask

Thanks Dev — helpful start. Quick clarifications: the CSV is raw API calls (not session-aggregated). Bursts are short-lived (typically 3–9 minutes) tied to product events. We do require interactive p95 <= 600ms for logged-in users — background churn (batch scoring, offline enrichment) can be delayed by up to 30s.

Model: we want to test a 13B quantized variant for the POC and compare to a fall-back cheaper 7B variant for background scoring. If you can show a recommended routing policy with explicit fallbacks and expected cost delta that would be ideal.

Also cc'ing ops so they can share a latency histogram if needed.

—Jen

From: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Jen Park <jen.park@lumina.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina POC - workload sample and quick sizing ask

Jen / team — summary and next steps below. Quoted key points from Dev's calculation and what we'll deliver by Friday.

Summary (recommended conservative POC footprint):
- Dedicated pool: start with 8 GPUs (13B quantized), configured with: burst autoscale up to 32 GPUs, pre-warmed KV cache for the top-10% frequent prefixes, and per-route concurrency caps to protect p95.
- Queueing & routing: interactive requests routed to an "interactive" routing tier with preemption enabled; background routes to a "batch" tier that accepts queued work with 30s max queue depth.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to 7B quantized variant for background tasks when burst headroom exhausted; fall back to regionally cheaper capacity only if cross-region latency still meets SLA.
- Estimated infra token cost (POC): $0.09 per 1k tokens (13B q) typical; $0.035 per 1k tokens for 7B q used as background replacement.

Deliverables by Friday:
1) A succinct one-page queueing diagram (queueing-diagram.png) showing routes and failover.
2) A tightened sizing spreadsheet with minute-level burst simulation and final recommended committed GPU count for the POC (sizing-estimate-v1.xlsx).
3) A short runbook for the POC team showing rollout steps and observability knobs (p95 tracer, token burn dashboard links).

Next steps: Rafael will sync with Jen to confirm burst histograms; Lumina ops to share latency histogram (if available). After we finalize numbers we'll prepare a short committed capacity quote for the POC (monthly reserved, with defined burst allowances).

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
